1336: \subsection{A shorter presentation in type $A$}
1337: \label{type-A-generators-subsection}
1338: 
1339: Starting with Theorem~\ref{general-J-generators}, our goal is to find
1340: an even smaller set of generators for the ideal $J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$
1341: within the coinvariant algebra, so that through (\ref{eqn:I_wconcat})
1342: we obtain an even shorter presentation of $I_w$ in type $A$.
1343: 
1344: First note that even though our proof of Theorem~\ref{general-J-generators}
1345: for all finite Coxeter groups was done
1346: in $\Bbbk[V]/(\Bbbk[V]^W_+)$ where the field $\Bbbk$ has characteristic zero,
1347: the same proof works in type $A$ more generally for the {\it integral}
1348: coinvariant algebra $H^\star(G/B,\ZZ)$. This follows since
1349: the Schubert polynomials $\{\schubp_w\}$ satisfy the integer
1350: coefficient versions of all of the requisite properties (a)-(g) used in Section~\ref{Hiller-section}.
1351: 
1352: 
1353: 
1354: The bigrassmannian $v_{r,s,t,n}$ described explicitly in \eqref{v-explicitly}
1355: is $r$-grassmannian, and corresponds to the $j \times i$ 
1356: rectangular partition $i^j$, where we define
1357: $$
1358: \begin{aligned}
1359: i&:=s-t+1,\\
1360: j&:=r-t+1.
1361: \end{aligned}
1362: $$
1363: 
1364: 
1365: When $u$ and $v$ are $r$-grassmannian and correspond respectively to
1366: partitions $\lambda$ and $\mu$, the Bruhat order relation $u \geq v$
1367: is equivalent to inclusion $\lambda \supseteq \mu$ of their Young
1368: diagrams, meaning that $\lambda_i \geq \mu_i$ for all $i$.  Thus
1369: Theorem~\ref{general-J-generators} says that $J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$ is
1370: generated as an ideal of $\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$ by
1371: \begin{equation}
1372: \label{step0-generators}
1373: \{\schubp_u: \Des(u) = \{(r,r+1)\}, \,\, u \geq v_{r,s,t,n}\}
1374: =\{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (n-r)^r \}.
1375: \end{equation}
1376: 
1377: This presentation from Theorem~\ref{general-J-generators} can be
1378: improved in type $A_{n-1}$ as follows:
1379: 
1380: \begin{theorem}
1381: \label{J-generators}
1382:   Given a bigrassmannian $v=v_{r,s,t,n}$ in type $A_{n-1}$ with $\schubp_v = s_{i^j}$, let
1383: $$
1384: \begin{aligned}
1385: a&:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\\
1386: b&:=\min(i,j).
1387: \end{aligned}
1388: $$
1389: 
1390: Then $J_v$ is generated as an ideal of 
1391: $H^{\star}(G/P_J, {\mathbb Z})\cong \Lambda/I_{r,n-r}$ by 
1392: \begin{equation}
1393: \label{generating-set-one}
1394: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq ((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}) \}.
1395: \end{equation}
1396: 
1397: Alternatively, $J_v$ is generated by 
1398: \begin{equation}
1399: \label{generating-set-two}
1400: \{ s_{\mu}: i^j \subseteq \mu \subseteq (i^j,b^a) \}.
1401: \end{equation}
1402: \end{theorem}
1403: 
1404: We delay our proof of Theorem~\ref{J-generators} until Section~\ref{minconjsection}.
1405: 
1406: \noindent
1407: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets \eqref{generating-set-one} and \eqref{generating-set-two} for $J_v$,
1408: the shapes $\mu$ indexing the generators $s_\mu$ run through an interval between
1409: the $j \times i$ rectangular shape $i^j$ and the disjoint union of $i^j$ with a 
1410: smaller rectangle of shape $a \times b$ or $b \times a$. 
1411: In \eqref{generating-set-one} the smaller rectangle is to the right
1412: of the rectangle $i^j$, with both top-justified, while in \eqref{generating-set-two} the 
1413: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle $i^j$, with both left-justified.  
1414: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size $\binom{a+b}{a}$
1415: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
1416: have generating function 
1417: $$
1418: \sum_\mu q^{|\mu|} = q^{ij} \qbin{a+b}{a},
1419: $$
1420: where $\qbin{a+b}{a}$ is a $q$-{\it binomial coefficient} or {\it Gaussian polynomial} 
1421: \cite[I.2 Exer. 3]{Macdonald}.
1422:

1426: \begin{example}
1427: \label{GR-comparison}
1428: We examine the special case where the bigrassmannian 
1429: $v:=v_{r,s,t,n}$ has $t$ equal to $r$ or $s$, so that the Schubert condition $C_{r,s,t}$
1430: in \ref{Schubert-condition} becomes an {\it inclusion} 
1431: $V_r \subseteq \CC^s$ or $V_r \supseteq \CC^s$.
1432: Schubert varieties $X_w$ in type $A$ for which 
1433: all Schubert conditions on $X_w$ take one of these two forms
1434: were called Schubert varieties {\it defined by inclusions} in
1435: \cite{GasharovReiner}.  That paper gave a presentation for the cohomology
1436: containing
1437: \begin{enumerate}
1438: \item[$\bullet$]
1439: for each inclusion condition $V_r \supseteq \CC^s$, 
1440: a set of $s$ generators for $J_v$ of the form 
1441: \begin{equation}
1442: \label{first-kind-of-inclusion}
1443: \{ e_m(x_1,\ldots,x_r) \}_{m=r-s+1,r-s+2,\ldots,r},
1444: \end{equation}
1445: \item[$\bullet$]
1446: and for each inclusion condition $V_r \subseteq \CC^s$, 
1447: a set of $r$ generators for $J_v$ of the form 
1448: \begin{equation}
1449: \{ e_m(x_r+1,\ldots,x_n) \}_{m=s-r+1,s-r+2,\ldots,n-r}.
1450: \end{equation}
1451: \end{enumerate}
1452: We compare this with the presentation for $J_v$ 
1453: in Theorem~\ref{J-generators},
1454: say for the inclusion conditions of the form 
1455: $V_r \supseteq \CC^s$, and using the 
1456: generators given in \eqref{generating-set-two}.
1457: 
1458: Since $t=s$, one has 
1459: $$
1460: \begin{aligned}
1461: i&=s-t+1=1\\
1462: j&=r-s+1\\
1463: b&=\min(i,j)=i=1\\
1464: a&=\min(n-r-1,s-1)
1465: \end{aligned}
1466: $$
1467: Hence  \eqref{generating-set-two} says
1468: that $J_v$ is generated by the set of $a+1$ Schur functions 
1469: $$
1470: \{ s_\mu: 1^{r-s+1} \subseteq \mu \subseteq 1^{a+r-s+1} \}
1471: =\{ e_m(x_1,\ldots,x_r) \}_{m=r-s+1,r-s+2,\ldots,a+r-s+1}
1472: $$
1473: which is exactly the first $a+1=\min(n-r,s)$ out of the $s$ generators 
1474: listed in \eqref{first-kind-of-inclusion}.  Hence Theorem~\ref{J-generators}
1475: provides a dramatic reduction in the size of the 
1476: generating set for $J_v$ whenever $n-r$ is small compared to $s$.
1477: 
1478: We remark also that the techniques utilized in \cite{GasharovReiner}
1479: seem very particular to the case where $X_w$ is defined by inclusions.
1480: We do not know how to use them for some alternate approach
1481: to the case of general $X_w$ considered in this paper.
1482: \end{example}

1489: \subsection{A minimality conjecture}
1490: \label{minconj}
1491: As we shall see in a moment, 
1492: our generators for $I_w$ are not minimal. However,
1493: we believe the following holds:
1494: 
1495: \begin{conjecture}
1496: \label{minimality-conjecture}
1497: The two generating sets for the ideal $J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$ given in Theorem~\ref{J-generators}
1498: are both minimal. 
1499: \end{conjecture}
1500: 
1501: Via computer, we have verified this conjecture for all bigrassmannian permutations
1502: where $r\leq 4$ and $n-r\leq 5$.
1503: 
1504: In fact, Conjecture~\ref{minimality-conjecture} indicates obstructions to short presentations of
1505: $H^{\star}(X_w)$ in general. We now give 
1506: a family of ideals that would require a large number of generators if the conjecture is true.
1507: 
1508: For a positive integer $m$, let $n=4m$, and consider in
1509: $W=S_n=S_{4m}$ the bigrassmannian $v_{r,s,t,n}$ that corresponds
1510: to $r=n-r=2m$ and $i=j=m$.  Then $a=b=m$, and $J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}(=I_{w_{r,s,t,n}})$ requires 
1511: \begin{equation}
1512: \label{eqn:badlowerbnd}
1513: \binom{2m}{m} \sim \frac{4^m}{\sqrt{\pi m}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}^{n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}
1514: \end{equation}
1515: generators according to Conjecture~\ref{minimality-conjecture}. 
1516: 
1517: The size of any minimal generating set of a homogeneous ideal is
1518: well-defined. This is implied by the following well-known fact:
1519: 
1520: \begin{proposition} 
1521: \label{prop:commalgfact}
1522: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and $\Lambda=\oplus_{n \geq 0}
1523: \Lambda_n$ a graded, connected $R$-algebra, meaning that $\Lambda_0
1524: =R$ and $\Lambda_i \Lambda_j \subset \Lambda_{i+j}$.  Let $M$ be a
1525: graded $\Lambda$-module, with degrees bounded below, meaning that
1526: $M=\oplus_{n \geq N} M_n$ for some $N \in \ZZ$, and $\Lambda_i M_j
1527: \subset M_{i+j}$.
1528: 
1529: Then a set of homogeneous elements $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ generate $M$ as a $\Lambda$-module
1530: if and only if their images $\{\bar{m_i}\}_{i=1}^t$ span $M/\Lambda_+ M$ as a $R$-module.
1531: In particular, $\{m_i\}_{i=1}^t$ form a minimal $\Lambda$-generating set with respect to
1532: inclusion for $M$ if and only if $\{\bar{m_i}\}_{i=1}^t$ form a minimal $R$-spanning
1533: set for $M/\Lambda_+ M$.  
1534: \end{proposition}
1535: 
1536: In our setting, the well-definedness follows by setting
1537: $\Lambda=\oplus_{n\geq 0}\Lambda_{n}$ to be the graded ring of
1538: symmetric functions with ${\mathbb Z}$ coefficients and setting
1539: $M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}$, so that the ${\mathbb Z}$-module $M/\Lambda_{+}M$
1540: is a finitely generated abelian group.

1545: %from Theorem~\ref{general-bound}.

1549: Thus we conjecture that this abelian group $M/ \Lambda_+ M$ requires
1550: $\binom{a+b}{a}$ generators, and in fact, we suspect that
1551: $M/\Lambda_{+}M\cong {\mathbb Z}^{\binom{a+b}{a}}$.  So far a proof
1552: has eluded us.

1924: \item[$\bullet$]

973: \begin{lemma}
974: The bigrassmannian permutations (other than the identity) are
975: parameterized by $r,s,t$ with $1\leq t \leq r,s \leq n$ and $t>r+s-n$.
976: Let $v_{r,s,t,n}$ denote the unique bigrassmannian permutation
977: $v_1\ldots v_n\in S_n$ such that
978: \begin{enumerate}
979: \item[$\bullet$] $\Des(v)=\{(r\leftrightarrow r+1)\}$ 
980: \item[$\bullet$] $\Des(v^{-1})=\{(s\leftrightarrow s+1)\}$, and
981: \item[$\bullet$] $v_t=s+1$.
982: \end{enumerate}
983: Then explicitly we have:
984: \begin{equation}
985: \label{v-explicitly}
986: \begin{aligned}
987: v_{r,s,t,n}&:=(1, 2, \ldots,t-1 , \\
988:         & \qquad s+1, s+2, \ldots, s+r-t+1, \\
989:         & \quad \qquad t, t+1,t+2, \ldots,s,\\
990:         & \qquad \qquad s+r-t+2,s+r-t+3,\ldots,n).
991: \end{aligned}
992: \end{equation}
993: \end{lemma}

146: A desirable feature of Borel's presentation is its shortness: since $W$
147: acts on $V^\star$ as a finite reflection group, by Chevalley's Theorem,
148: the $W$-invariants $\Bbbk[V]^W$ are a polynomial algebra
149: $\Bbbk[f_1,\ldots,f_n]$, where $n:=\dim_\Bbbk V$ is the rank of
150: $G$ \cite[Section~3.5]{humphreys}.  Hence Borel's presentation shows
151: that $H^\star(G/B)$ is a complete intersection as it has $n$ generators and
152: $n$ relations.
153: 
154:  There is a second way to describe $H^{\star}(G/B)$ arising from
155:  a cell decomposition of $G/B$. One has
156: $$
157: \begin{array}{rll}
158: G&=\bigsqcup_{w \in W} BwB & \text{(Bruhat decomposition)}\\
159: G/B&=\bigsqcup_{w \in W} X_w^\circ & \text{(Schubert cell decomposition), with}\\ 
160: X_w^\circ&:=BwB/B \cong \CC^{\ell(w)} &\text{ (open Schubert cell)}.  
161: \end{array}
162: $$ Here $\ell(w)$ denotes the Coxeter group length of $w$ under the
163: Coxeter system $(W,S)$, where $S$ are the reflections in the simple
164: roots $\Pi$ among the positive roots $\Phi^+$ 
165: within the natural root system $\Phi$ associated to our Lie pinning.  
166: This gives a
167: $CW$-decomposition for $G/B$ in which all cells have even real
168: dimension.  Hence the fundamental homology classes $[X_w]$ of their
169: closures $X_w:=\overline{X_w^\circ}$, the {\bf Schubert varieties},
170: form a $\ZZ$-basis for the integral homology $H_\star(G/B)$, and their
171: (Kronecker) duals $\sigma_w:=[X_w]^\star$ form the dual $\ZZ$-basis for
172: the integral cohomology $H^\star(G/B)$.
173: 
174: The above facts lead to an {\it a priori} presentation
175: for $H^\star(X_w)$; see also \cite[Cor. 4.4]{Carrell} and
176: \cite[Prop. 2.1]{GasharovReiner}:  The Schubert variety $X_w$ is the
177: union of the Schubert cells $X_u^\circ$ for which $u \leq w$ in the
178: {\it (strong) Bruhat order}; hence it inherits a cell decomposition
179: from the flag variety.  Consequently, the map on cohomology
180: $$
181: H^\star(G/B) \rightarrow H^\star(X_w)
182: $$
183: induced by including $X_w \hookrightarrow G/B$ is surjective 
184: with kernel

187: I_w:=\Bbbk\text{-span of }\{ \sigma_u: u \not\leq w \}.
188: \end{equation}

10: ## 1. The formally stated conjecture
11: 
12: ### Minimality conjecture
13: 
14: For a type-\(A_{n-1}\) bigrassmannian permutation \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), Theorem 5.4 supplies two generating sets for the ideal \(J_v\). The authors conjecture:
15: 
16: > **Conjecture.** The two generating sets for the ideal \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) given in Theorem 5.4 are both minimal.
17: 
18: Here, if \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the parameters are
19: 
20: \[
21: a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\qquad b=\min(i,j).
22: \]
23: 
24: Theorem 5.4 gives the two sets
25: 
26: \[
27: \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}
28: \]
29: 
30: and
31: 
32: \[
33: \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}.
34: \]
35: 
36: Each contains
37: 
38: \[
39: \binom{a+b}{a}
40: \]
41: 
42: generators. “Minimal” means that no proper subset still generates \(J_v\).
43: 
44: **Primary-source location:** `sources/0809.2981v2.tex`, lines 1380–1421 and 1489–1499.
45: 
46: ## 2. Evidence reported by the authors
47: 
48: The authors state that they verified the conjecture computationally for all bigrassmannian permutations satisfying
49: 
50: \[
51: r\leq 4,\qquad n-r\leq 5.
52: \]
53: 
54: **Primary-source location:** lines 1501–1502.
55: 
56: ## 3. Stronger suspected formulation
57: 
58: Set \(M=J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\), and let \(\Lambda_+\) denote the positive-degree part of the ring of symmetric functions. The authors further conjecture that
59: 
60: \[
61: M/\Lambda_+M
62: \]
63: 
64: requires \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators. They suspect the stronger structural statement
65: 
66: \[
67: M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}.
68: \]
69: 
70: This is presented in prose rather than as a second numbered conjecture. The authors write that a proof had eluded them.
71: 
72: **Primary-source location:** lines 1517–1552.
73: 
74: ## 4. Consequence of the conjecture
75: 
76: Take \(n=4m\) and the family for which \(a=b=m\). If the minimality conjecture is true, the corresponding ideal requires
77: 
78: \[
79: \binom{2m}{m}
80: \sim \frac{4^m}{\sqrt{\pi m}}
81: =\frac{\sqrt{2}^{\,n+2}}{\sqrt{\pi n}}
82: \]
83: 
84: generators. This gives an exponential lower bound and shows that uniformly short presentations of \(H^*(X_w)\) cannot be expected in general, even in type \(A\).
85: 
86: **Primary-source location:** lines 1504–1515; see also the introductory discussion at lines 355–364.
87: 
88: ## 5. Related open question
89: 
90: The final section asks:
91: 
92: > Can one find a minimal generating set for the ideal \(I_w\) in type \(A_{n-1}\)?
93: 
94: The authors ask whether this can at least be done for subclasses already known to admit generating sets of size \(n^2\), including:
95: 
96: 1. Schubert varieties defined by inclusions, characterized there by avoidance of
97:    \(\{4231,35142,42513,351624\}\);
98: 2. smooth Schubert varieties, characterized by avoidance of \(\{3412,4231\}\).
99: 
100: This is an open question, not another formally labeled conjecture.
101: 
102: **Primary-source location:** lines 1897–1935.
103:

110: | Minimal generating sets for general \(I_w\) in type \(A\) | Formally labeled open question |
